summary: Wooden screw-pile light in the middle of Mobile Bay, lit December 1885; automated 1935; closed to the public, with repairs under way in 2026.

access.note: Not open to the public; offshore in the bay and best seen by boat (South Alabama News, 2026; LighthouseFriends).

events.note: Prefabricated in the North; ironwork arrived at Fort Morgan or Mobile Point in 1885; erected on screw piles
Established December 1885; LighthouseFriends and the Keeper's Log give 1 December 1885
Structure settled about seven and a half feet on 12 September 1885 during erection; no structural damage
Nomination: rebuilt and believed a duplicate of the original. LighthouseFriends: lens and lantern room removed, two acetylene lights on a pole. Sources differ
Hurricane of 1916 ended continuous manning of the station (Keeper's Log)
Automated by the Coast Guard; no keeper after the mid-1930s (nomination; South Alabama News)
Coast Guard declared the structure a hazard to navigation (Keeper's Log)
GSA gave permission to demolish; Mobile Bar Pilots and others protested and the demolition was dropped

State nomination signed 20 September 1974; the keeper attestation line reads 'PEC 2 7 1974' in the OCR. LighthouseFriends says the listing was in 1975; the station record's 30 December 1974 is not in the cited sources.
Navy Reserve Mobile Construction Battalion 14 (SeaBees) began restoration work
Centennial restoration by volunteers, October to December 1985, with Coast Guard transport
Restoration under a $349,400 contract from the Alabama Historical Commission (LighthouseFriends)
Alabama Historical Commission voted against moving the light ashore to Battleship Park
$270,000 restoration including structural repairs and new windows
A shrimp boat ran into the lighthouse, bending a metal support piling and breaking tie-rods
Repairs to roof, walkway and other parts since late June 2026; price given as $1.2 million

corrections.current: 33 deg 16.1 min N, 88 deg 0.4 min W (USLHS Mobile Middle Bay)
corrections.proposed: 30 deg 26 min N, 88 deg 1 min W (station record and nomination)
corrections.why: The USLHS place record puts the Mobile Middle Bay light about 300 km north of the bay, which is a transcription error; the station record is the right position. Noted for the archive, not a change to this record.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Mobile Bay light station was established in December 1885 (nomination); the Keeper's Log and LighthouseFriends give 1 December 1885. The station record's 1885 is consistent. No conflict remains on the year.
The nomination uses Middle Bay Light and Mobile Bay Light interchangeably; the USLHS archive uses Mobile Middle Bay. Same station.
The archive roster gives Cuthbert as head keeper to 1893 and Terreson from 1893; LighthouseFriends gives Cuthbert to 1903 and Terreson from 1903. The story states both and does not choose.

notes_for_editor: Moderate-to-rich evidence: the NRHP nomination (1974), the Keeper's Log feature (Spring 1986, unsigned), two 1903/1905 Montgomery Advertiser items, LighthouseFriends (copyrighted compiled history, cited for facts and short quotes only), a 2026 South Alabama News article, and the USLHS roster. Disagreements now stated in the story: distance (1905 paper: eighteen miles below Mobile; Keeper's Log: about 15 miles south of the harbor; LighthouseFriends: 14.3 miles north of Mobile Point); first lighting (December 1885 per the nomination, and 1 December 1885 per the Log and LighthouseFriends; September 1885 per the 2026 article); head keeper dates (archive vs LighthouseFriends); 1905 change (nomination vs LighthouseFriends); 1935 automation/electrification (nomination, LighthouseFriends) vs lantern conversion just before World War II (Log); 2008 vs 2009 move proposal (LighthouseFriends vs 2026 article); lens location (LighthouseFriends: with the Coast Guard in Mobile; 2026 article: on display at the Fort Morgan Museum); lantern-room location (National Maritime Museum per LighthouseFriends; GulfQuest per the 2026 article). The 1916 mother-and-baby story is LighthouseFriends only and says 'during World War I'; it names no keeper. The Keeper's Log says 'a replica of the Hooper's Strait Lighthouse'; the nomination says 'reputedly' and 'off the Maryland Coast'. The USCG Historian's Middle Bay article could not be read. The Alabama Historical Commission station page returned only its title. The South Alabama News article says the light 'still serves working boaters as a local waypoint'; the story does not claim it is lit. Lighthouse Board reports for 1885-1890 are not in the local corpus, so there is no official-report source for construction. Architect: no source read names one; the story names none. Modern restoration staff are not named. A former Coast Guard crewman quoted by LighthouseFriends is not named (service in the 1960s). The roster place's latitude in the USLHS record is a transcription error (see corrections).
